To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an active anycast RTTB server selection technique is better than a static round robin server-selection technique.

the active anycast method performs better than static round robin in terms of the response time, throughput, and fairness, and the active anycast with a single server selection method performs better than the active anycast without a single server selection technique in terms of response time, throughput and fairness.
the RTT based anycast server selection method outperforms the static round robin selection method in all the performance metrics that we consider.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and performance evaluation of an active network based server selection technique that can be used for load balancing, server failover, and server selection in a quality of service (QoS) environment.

the following: (1) the performance of RTT based server selections in a specific network environment (2) the impact of the number of servers and the load on the network on server selection performance (3) the impact of active network on server selection and (4) the impact of server selection on the network performance.
developing an active anycast based server selection technique to improve the performance and reliability of Internet services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
an active network based anycast RTT server selection technique performs better than a static server selection technique in all the network conditions tested in our simulation.
the anycast method with RTT based server-selection is more efficient in terms of response time and throughput and is also more robust in terms of server failure than the static round robin method.
the anycast based RTT based server-selection method is a viable alternative to the static round robin method in the case of a geographically dispersed replicated architecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RTT based server selections are better suited for the active network environment than the round robin server selection.

the RTT based server load balancing techniques are more effective than the static round robin method and that the active anycast RTTs are more effective than passive RTTs in terms of the performance of the network layer anycasts.
the RTT based server selections are better than static server selections in the case of a localized web cluster architecture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a RTT based server load balancing method can be effectively used in an anycast based server selection technique to provide a better quality of service to the users.
the RTT based server load balancing technique can provide significant performance improvement over the static round robin selection technique in a localized cluster of servers.

the RTT based server-selection technique can provide better performance in terms of the average response time and the response time variance than the static server-selection technique in a network where the server locations and the client locations are known.
